neighbours.label: ' cent' in 'per cent' (percent written as two words)
fire: The bank charged him a rate of nine per cent on the loan.
Prices rose by about four per cent in the first quarter.
Nearly eighty per cent of the voters came to the polls.
The tax was raised to twelve per cent by the new king.
Only ten per cent of the seeds grew in that poor soil.
Money was then worth six per cent a year in the colony.
Sales fell by two per cent after the storm.
He offered the farmers fifteen per cent of the crop.
quiet: The bank charged him a fee of nine dollars on the loan.
Prices rose by about four percent in the first quarter.
Nearly eighty thousand of the voters came to the polls.
The tax was raised to twelve shillings by the new king.
Only ten bags of the seeds grew in that poor soil.
Money was then worth six pence a year in the colony.
Sales fell by two percent after the storm.
He offered the farmers fifteen acres of the crop.
